summary: Summarizes the issues in the relationship between the IETF and the Internet Society, as discussed by the Poised working group, in order to gauge consensus. It was replaced by RFC 8712.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 2031 summarizes proposed ways for the IETF and the Internet Society to divide responsibilities, while keeping the IETF responsible for Internet standards and their technical content. It was written to gauge consensus, not to establish a formal process, and was later replaced by RFC 8712.

questions: what is the relationship between ietf and isoc
subtitle: A summary of proposed boundaries between IETF and ISOC responsibilities

tldr.problem: As the IETF grew, it faced non-technical work and needed to describe how responsibilities could be shared with ISOC.
tldr.mechanism: The memo summarizes Poised Working Group recommendations for discussion, including IETF responsibility for technical standards and ISOC support for selected legal and organizational matters.
tldr.outcome: This informational memo was intended to gauge consensus and was later replaced by RFC 8712.

sections.title: Why Discuss the Relationship
sections.content:
The IETF develops and maintains Internet standards through working groups, discussion and rough consensus. As participation and responsibility grew, legal and organizational issues became a larger part of its work.

The Poised Working Group recommended moving non-technical issues that could safely be moved to a related organization. This memo summarizes those recommendations so the community can assess consensus and discuss the division of responsibilities.
sections.plainLanguage: The IETF develops Internet standards, but its growth also brought more legal and organizational work. This memo summarizes proposals for handling some of that work outside the IETF.

sections.title: The Proposed Boundary
sections.content:
The main boundary is that the IETF remains responsible for developing and ensuring the quality of Internet standards. The memo says ISOC has no influence on the standards process, standards or their technical content beyond the roles described in the proposal.

The proposed support includes a legal umbrella for IETF officers, protection for the RFC series so documents can be freely distributed but not altered, and legal protection in intellectual-property disputes. ISOC would also assist parts of the standards process, including appointments, approvals and appeals.
sections.plainLanguage: The proposal keeps technical standards decisions with the IETF. ISOC would provide specified legal and organizational support without deciding the technical content.

sections.title: Openness and Safeguards
sections.content:
The memo says official subgroups should either be open to anyone or have documented membership restrictions and an open nomination or election process. It also says ISOC should use public discussion and consensus when developing policies that may affect its role or Internet technical work.

The RFC discusses risks of involving another organization and alternatives, including having the IETF handle everything itself. It argues for clearly defined limits on ISOC's role, while acknowledging that some risk is unavoidable.
sections.plainLanguage: The recommendations call for open participation or clearly documented selection rules. They also propose public discussion and clear limits on ISOC's involvement.

sections.title: An Informational Discussion Memo
sections.content:
RFC 2031 states that it has no formal status and is not intended to receive formal status. The working documents from the Poised Working Group were expected to become the formal documents; this memo's role was to summarize recommendations and gauge consensus.

The unit metadata records RFC 8712 as the document that later obsoleted this memo.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC presents recommendations for discussion, not binding rules. RFC 8712 later replaced it.
